thread:
sara: Heads-up: prototype for a "tenant-local" control plane landed in staging. We need a short design check focused on DNS handoff guarantees and cert rotation load on customer KMS. TL;DR: want low-risk activation path and a way to avoid KMS storms.

ben: Congrats on the POC. Two recipe-level ideas: (1) verification token for glue records so we don't trust partial delegation, (2) adaptive cert batching that widens when KMS shows signs of pressure.

otto: +1. For glue verification: after we request NS delegation, the customer adds a TXT token at _redwood-delegate.example.com. We probe public resolvers and only proceed when the token is visible from >=3 vantage points. That avoids ambiguous partial delegation.

hema: For certs: prefer a push model where the central controller prepares bundles and pushes them to the tenant CP over an authenticated channel. Bundling reduces unwraps. Also consider per-tenant envelope keys so multiple certs can be unwrapped with a single KMS call.

sara: Push model makes sense; what about tenants that require manual allowlist of new cert thumbprints?

ben: Add a flag in tenant profile: "activation_mode": ["auto","manual"]. In manual mode controller emits an "awaiting-allowlist" event with fingerprint and waits for customer webhook/console ack. We should show human-friendly thumbprints in the UI.

otto: Failure modes: partial delegation + weight flip can cause split-responses. Suggest we require probe consensus before we change weight. Flow: provision CP (state: ready, weight=0) -> request token+delegation -> verify token visible >=3 resolvers -> run health probes against new CP from our probe fleet -> if probes pass >=90% then set weight->100. All actions reversible.

hema: And a safety net: if probes disagree (some probes still hit old NS) we keep weight at 0 and enable a short synthetic answer window for endpoint A/AAAA only, TTL 30s, for up to 4 minutes. This limits user-visible downtime while delegation converges.

ben: On batching: controller should dynamically choose batch_window = min(120s, base + alpha * current_kms_latency). Start base=30s, alpha tuned by ops. Also cap batch size to avoid huge envelope bundles (default 200 certs). Emit metrics: chosen_batch_window, batch_cert_count, kms_unwraps_saved.

otto: KMS circuit-breaker: if unwrap error rate >2% sustained over 3m OR latency >P95_threshold, flip to degraded mode: stop new rotations, extend existing cert TTLs by X, and page SecOps. Also prevent >N concurrent delegations per-org (default 4).

hema: Operational checklist (short): 1) verify delegate token visible from 3+ external resolvers; 2) confirm glue NS entries in registrar UI (where applicable); 3) KMS quota check and envelope-key availability; 4) enable synthetic DNS fallback; 5) run blue/green weight flip gating on health probes; 6) monitor batch metrics and KMS errors.

sara: Example of a controller rotate request (push model):

curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/1234/push-rotate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kind":"leaf","activate_after":"probe_ok","activation_mode":"auto"}'

Response: {"op_id":"op-20260323-01","estimated_window_s":"45"} (async)

ben: Nice. For the token check implement exponential backoff for probes: try immediately, then 10s, 30s, 60s, stop after 5 fails and mark delegation as failed. That reduces noisy retries.

otto: Also add a small telemetry event "delegate_verification_latency" and histogram. We can tune registrar/registrant guidance based on real-world delays.

hema: mTLS termination placement: suggest default terminate at tenant CP with short-lived client certs issued by the push, but support an optional minimal handshake agent customers can run in their VPC for networks that don't allow outbound mTLS to our CPs. The agent only does cert handshakes and liveness, not routing.

sara: Any runbook entries for rollback during a partial activation?

ben: Keep activation idempotent and maintain a commit marker: cp_state{candidate_id, weight}. If we detect partial DNS propagation or health regression, revert weight to previous and mark candidate unsuitable. Also emit a rollback_count metric.

otto: One more: protect against registrar mistakes by requiring a secondary-verifier step: after token found, we do a NTP-synced timestamp challenge to the CP and include that in the registrar instructions so we can correlate apply-time vs propagation. Small but helpful for debugging.

sara: OK action items: ben+hema draft adaptive-batcher + manual activation flow, otto document token verification and probe heuristics, I'll wire push API and staging fallback. Follow-up RFC next Tue 9:30. Thanks! :raised_hands:
